title: Nocked Arrows
text: Tatan! Tan! Panda whipped out short blades hidden in the hems and collar of her outfit, wedging them deftly between each finger before sending them flying with practiced ease. Riska had done something similar with throwing knives before, but Panda handled just about anything with remarkable dexterity.
“Bu-bu-buhee!”

Lazy Pig was working the crowd with a microphone in hand, hyping them up at the top of her lungs. A brisk little drumbeat rang out, and the audience’s attention locked onto the spotlit Panda and her subordinate strapped to the target board. Stan, stan—Panda hurled her knives one after another, tracing the outline of her subordinate’s body with razor-thin margins. Quite the feat of acrobatics, I say. A proper knife-throwing artiste, that Panda. Incidentally, Panda’s grandfather used to do something similar, though his style had been far more slapdash. Itsuki, meanwhile, peered out from atop Father’s head, staring intently at the whole performance.
“Itsuki, I think you could pull off an act like that, don’t you? You’re good at it, right?”
“Something at that level, sure, I could do it without even trying. That said… whether I feel like entertaining the people of this country is another matter. Let me think about it.”
“I think it’d be good for you to show that ‘public face’ in the show, so I’m hoping for a positive answer.”
The public face: a crack squirrel-beastman marksman in the circus. The hidden face: an assassin picking off Melromarc nobles in the shadows.
“If I recall, near the end there’s supposed to be a miss, right?”
“Yep. After that, the human throws similarly and lands it clean to close things out. There’s a noticeable difference in applause between when everything succeeds and when there’s a failure mixed in.”
This was Melromarc, after all. Plenty of customers wouldn’t be satisfied unless the script had the demi-humans or beastmen fail at some point in the act.
“Kyain—!?”

Right on cue, Panda “missed” her throw, and the knife thudded into her subordinate with a spray of stage blood. The failure-knives, of course, came with a little blood-packet gimmick built in. After a flustered bit of acting, Panda threw another knife that grazed her subordinate’s cheek, adding insult to injury before the poor thing tumbled off the ball and dropped to her knees. All part of the act, naturally. Funnily enough, during rehearsals Panda had hit the mark with yawn-inducing precision every single time—missing on purpose seemed like a foreign concept to her. Afterward, one of the monster dealer’s subordinates would step in to finish the routine with a series of perfectly landed throws. Apparently during rehearsals he’d been so awed by Panda’s skill that their relationship had flipped—more like a student learning from a master.
“Bu-bu-hi-bu!”

Lazy Pig’s announcement drew applause, bringing the knife-throwing act to a close. The target board, with Panda’s subordinate still tied to it, was wheeled backstage with a clatter, and the ropes were finally undone.
“Good work out there. Let me patch you up.”
“Yes sir! Finally got to play the target for Big Sis—it was fun, sir!”
“Glad to hear it.”
Father immediately set to work healing the injured spots with recovery magic.

In a blur, Itsuki drew his bow and fired, nocking an arrow squarely into the handle of every single knife Panda had thrown. The monster dealer’s subordinate came stumbling back to check on the target board, only to freeze in shock at the sight of it, utterly transformed.
“Just fooling around. Don’t mind it.”

His tone practically dripped with the smug insinuation that anyone could pull off something so simple. Not exactly a great first impression. But then again, Itsuki being Itsuki, what else would you expect?

“Yeah, I figured this kind of act suits Itsuki. If it leaves a bad impression here, maybe it’d be better to have you perform over in Zeltoble instead. They don’t need the ‘failure’ bit over there. You could take Emia-san on as an assistant.”
Father, seemingly unbothered in the slightest, offered the suggestion as though genuinely impressed.
“……I’ll consider it. Though I won’t be tying Emia-san to a target board. Though knowing her, she’d probably volunteer for it.”
“Well, she does seem eager to make herself useful somehow, so try not to leave her hanging too long, alright? Keeping the village kids’ enthusiasm in check on our end is a handful as it is.”
He meant Big Sister and the others—lately they’d been performing in the Zeltoble shows with some regularity. Simply put, as a circus, Zeltoble’s audience received it far more warmly.
“The desire to work hard for someone’s sake… that matters, you know.”
“……I suppose it does.”
Itsuki, in his usual can’t-be-honest way, seemed unable to argue and simply conceded the point.
“Next up is the martial demonstration. Who’s the main act this time?”
“Me and Shion.”
Éclair arrived in her circus outfit—rather thin fabric—alongside Crocodile Guy, wielding his massive battle-axe.
“Right, Eclair-san, Shion, do your best.”
“Leave it to me.”
“I still think it isn’t necessary for Eclair-sama to participate in something like this, but…”
“Don’t say such things. I wish to perform. If I don’t, am I not simply a freeloader?”
“No, that’s not what I—”

Éclair and Crocodile Guy were bickering in hushed voices. True, Éclair served as the training instructor within the circus, but in terms of raw skill she still fell short of Panda’s grandfather and the old crone. Her value existed largely as a symbol of hope for the demi-humans within Melromarc until the Queen’s return. So she took part in the martial demonstration as a way of contributing to the circus, however small. Incidentally, this particular act was quite popular among those in the circus wanting to participate. It started with the pairing of Panda’s grandfather and the old crone, then Éclair and Crocodile Guy, and sometimes even I joined in. I usually faced off against Wolf, spinning my spear about flashily while parrying his leaping attacks. Though it was an act that required a certain restraint—I couldn’t let the Melromarc nobility catch wind of just how skilled I truly was, so it needed to look somewhat clumsy while still appearing flashy. A delicate balance, I say. As a bit of added trivia, the most popular pairing by far was Éclair in her skimpy outfit—the reason being, apparently, a great many lecherous men wanting an eyeful of her figure. Of course, since the performance took place further back on the stage as well, hardly anyone declined to participate.
“It’s simply that the eyes of those whose only aim is ogling Eclair-sama’s body are unpleasant to witness.”
Crocodile Guy clenched his fists tightly.

“Hmph. The notion that anyone would harbor such base desires toward me is unthinkable. And if such a person exists, they are nothing but a disgraceful fool wasting their attention on trivialities. Should any noble prove to be such a person, I need only remember his face and see that he receives his due punishment eventually.”
“Yes, ma’am!”
Crocodile Guy nodded firmly at Éclair’s words. Father watched the exchange with a smile.
“Shion really does come alive when he’s with Eclair-san, doesn’t he? Makes you wonder if he’s got a bit of a thing for her.”
Father teased, a mischievous grin playing at his lips as he addressed Crocodile Guy.
“I merely said what I thought—my feelings toward Eclair-sama are nothing but loyalty. M-more importantly, is there some sort of problem?”
“Nope, none so far. Alright, Shion. Go show off your strength alongside Eclair-san—flashy, but valiant.”
“Y-yes, sir!”
Encouraged by Father, Crocodile Guy nodded deeply.
“It seems he has already chosen the one to whom he pledges his loyalty. I am pleased, Shion.”
Éclair smiled at the exchange between Father and Crocodile Guy. Father watched the two of them dash off toward the stage, footsteps quick and light.

“Man, Eclair-san and Shion really do make quite the picture when they stand together, don’t they? Kind of a beauty-and-the-beast vibe. What a cool combo—like a crack noble swordswoman and a hard-boiled, world-weary lizardman. I could get behind that.”

Those backstage watched Father share this opinion with expressions somewhere between fondness and exasperation. Why was it that I felt the same strange atmosphere here that I used to feel back in my school days?
“Indeed. Eclair-sama suits Shion perfectly.”
“Vof! Perfectly! We’re with Naofumi-sama!”
“Yeah! We’ll fight alongside Iwatani-sama!”

Wolf and Rabbit Guy were saying something along those lines. But standing beside Father—that spot belonged to Filo-tan and me! In the depths of my memory, Big Sister radiated bloodlust, demanding to know why she’d been left out of the lineup, but I chose not to pay it any mind!
